title: FBR Integration Deadline
metaDescription: Discover the FBR integration deadline and learn how to comply with FBR IRIS and Sales Tax Act regulations to avoid penalties of up to PKR 500,000
content:
What is FBR integration deadline?

FBR integration deadline refers to the deadline set by the Federal Board of Revenue (FBR) for businesses to integrate their Point of Sale (POS) systems with the FBR's IRIS portal.

Introduction to FBR Integration Deadline

The FBR has extended the deadline for sales tax registrants to integrate their POS systems with the FBR's IRIS portal. This extension is aimed at facilitating businesses in complying with the new regulations.

Key Takeaway: FBR integration deadline has been extended.

Understanding FBR IRIS Portal

The FBR IRIS portal is a web-based system that allows businesses to register, file tax returns, and make payments online. To comply with the FBR IRIS portal, businesses must integrate their POS systems with the portal through an API.

For instance, a pharmacy in Karachi can use the FBR IRIS API to generate a QR invoice for each sale, which can then be used to claim input tax credit.

Step-by-Step Guide to FBR Integration

Here are the steps to follow for FBR integration:

  1. Register for FBR IRIS portal: Businesses must register for the FBR IRIS portal and obtain a User ID and password.
  2. Obtain an API token: Businesses must obtain an API token from the FBR IRIS portal, which is used to authenticate API requests.
  3. Configure POS system: Businesses must configure their POS system to generate QR invoices and integrate with the FBR IRIS portal.
  4. Test API integration: Businesses must test the API integration to ensure that it is working correctly.
  5. Go live with FBR IRIS integration: Once the integration is tested, businesses can go live with the FBR IRIS integration.
  6. Monitor and resolve issues: Businesses must monitor the integration and resolve any issues that may arise.

Real-World Example of FBR Integration

For example, a retail business in Lahore can use the FBR IRIS API to generate QR invoices for each sale. The business can then use the QR invoices to claim input tax credit and reduce their tax liability.

To illustrate, let's consider a textile business in Faisalabad that has integrated its POS system with the FBR IRIS portal. The business can generate QR invoices for each sale and use the invoices to claim input tax credit.

Common Mistakes to Avoid

Here are some common mistakes to avoid when integrating with the FBR IRIS portal:

  • Incorrect API token: Using an incorrect API token can result in authentication errors.
  • Insufficient testing: Insufficient testing can result in integration issues.
  • Inadequate monitoring: Inadequate monitoring can result in unresolved issues.
  • Non-compliance with FBR regulations: Non-compliance with FBR regulations can result in penalties of up to PKR 500,000.
  • Failure to obtain STRN: Failure to obtain a Sales Tax Registration Number (STRN) can result in penalties.

Deeper Insight into FBR IRIS API

The FBR IRIS API uses a token-based authentication system, where businesses must obtain a token and use it to authenticate API requests. The token is valid for a certain period, after which it expires and must be renewed.

For instance, the FBR IRIS API uses a JSON Web Token (JWT) to authenticate API requests. The JWT token is valid for 30 minutes, after which it expires and must be renewed.

Benefits of FBR Integration

Here are the benefits of FBR integration:

  • Reduced tax liability: FBR integration can help businesses reduce their tax liability by claiming input tax credit.
  • Improved compliance: FBR integration can help businesses improve their compliance with FBR regulations.
  • Increased efficiency: FBR integration can help businesses increase their efficiency by automating tax-related tasks.
  • Better record-keeping: FBR integration can help businesses improve their record-keeping by generating QR invoices for each sale.
  • Reduced penalties: FBR integration can help businesses reduce penalties by ensuring compliance with FBR regulations.
